column1: # Which lists of an image that builds arrays may be arrays (lib/lrc/Classes.rsd "Which lists may be arrays", `arrClassesOf`;
# lib/lrc/FromWire.rsd "The cells of a list that is no array"). A list that the classes do not mark is not asked for its cells, so a
# mark that is lost shows where an array arrives: its object is read as a cell. The rows: what makes an array marks nothing (a push
# or a write at an index; the array of a list or a slice); nothing may be an array; the cells asked of a list do not hold the list's
# elements (an array of arrays made a list); what is stored in a node's object does not reach its field; a read of a node's field is
# not the field; and every list that may be an array is the one left without its cells. The program that meets each of them is
# instruments/lrc-host/ProgArrFlow.rsd (row arrflow of Images.tsv): there each way a value flows has a function of its own that
# takes the list apart. A function that several ways share is marked through any one of them: the program's first form had one
# such function for all, and rows 2, 4, 5 and 6 changed nothing that a check saw.
# Not rows, and why. They leave more lists asked for their cells and no value changes: the cells asked of a list joined to the list
# (`primArrToList` under `cx.arr`); a constant joined like a variable (`Oc.consts`); the length and the equality of lists followed as
# functions (`ocCall`); a node's read without its tag (`layTagged`), which is then a read of every tag's field. No image has them: a
# magnitude that is an array (the stage's functions of a number followed as functions), an object from an expression the walk does
# not follow, a write into a field (`opSet`), a class "Layout" merged that holds an array (`ocNodeProjRound`), a class of cells of
# both shapes (`ocKindsBad`, `ocTailRound`).
